item.title: Iran War Live Updates: Trump Says Iran to Allow More Oil Ships Through Strait of Hormuz
item.summary: Two Chinese ships crossed the strait in an initial sign that Iran could be relaxing its de facto blockade, according to a ship-tracking platform. President Trump said that “great progress” was being made toward a deal, even as he threatened Tehran with intense attacks.

item.title: Myanmar’s Military Leader Moves One Step Closer to Becoming President
item.summary: Senior Gen. Min Aung Hlaing stepped down as commander in chief and is expected to be installed as the next civilian leader of the country by its rubber-stamp Parliament.

item.title: In Australia, Victoria and Tasmania Waive Transit Fares as Fuel Prices Soar
item.summary: The measures in Victoria and Tasmania are temporary, but show how far and how intensely the oil shock from the war in Iran has spread.

item.title: A Toothless Iran? Missile and Drone Strikes Show It Can Still Inflict Pain.
item.summary: A wave of strikes across the Middle East in recent days shows that Iran has not lost the capacity to retaliate.

item.title: Ukraine Finalizes Air Defense Deals With Gulf Nations Amid War in Mideast
item.summary: The Ukrainian president visited the Middle East, where he sought to shift his country from a recipient of military aid to a supplier.

item.title: Trump Claims ‘Regime Change’ in Iran Is Already Complete
item.summary: President Trump suggested that Iran’s current leaders were “much more reasonable” as he sought to show progress in his war aims. Despite a month of U.S.-Israeli attacks, Iran’s government, led by clerics and the Revolutionary Guards, appears firmly in control.

item.title: Israel to Vote on Death Penalty Targeting Palestinians Guilty of Lethal Attacks
item.summary: The bill is broadly popular and expected to pass. Critics say it would strip away many of the safeguards intended to preserve due process, including the possibility of a pardon.

item.title: Australian Police Kill Man Suspected of Slaying 2 Officers
item.summary: The fugitive, who was trained in surviving in the bush, had been on the run since a deadly confrontation last August with officers who had come to execute a search warrant.

item.title: On Iran’s Rugged Frontier, Kurds Yearn to Join the Fight
item.summary: These groups’ dream has long been to establish federal autonomy, akin to that of their fellow Kurds in Iraq. With Iran’s leaders battered and degraded, they hope their moment has come.

item.title: Can the ‘Dubai Dream’ Survive the War? Residents Say Life Goes On.
item.summary: The Emirates’ largest city pitched itself to foreign workers and tourists as a sun-soaked safe haven in a volatile region. War has challenged that image.
